Pirathon@Jdg.12.13-1Ch.description: Pirathon was a town in the hill country of Ephraim, associated with the judge Abdon and two of David's mighty men, Benaiah and Hiddai.
Pirathon@Jdg.12.13-1Ch.name: Pirathon

Pisgah@Num.21.20-Jos.description: Pisgah, or the slopes of Pisgah, was a mountain range in Moab where Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death.
Pisgah@Num.21.20-Jos.name: Pisgah

Pishon@Gen.2.11.description: Pishon was one of the four rivers that flowed from the river in the Garden of Eden, encircling the land of Havilah, which was known for its gold, bdellium, and onyx.
Pishon@Gen.2.11.name: Pishon

Pisidia@Act.13.14-.description: Pisidia was a mountainous region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel during their first missionary journey.
Pisidia@Act.13.14-.name: Pisidia

Pispa@1Ch.7.38.description: Pispa, a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles.
Pispa@1Ch.7.38.name: Pispa

Pithom@Exo.1.11.description: Pithom was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Rameses.
Pithom@Exo.1.11.name: Pithom

Pithon@1Ch.8.35-.description: Pithon, a descendant of King Saul, mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.
Pithon@1Ch.8.35-.name: Pithon

Pleiades@Job.9.9-Amo.description: The Pleiades are a star cluster mentioned in <ref="Job.9.9; 38:31">Job.9.9; 38:31</ref> as a display of God's creative power and in <ref="Amo.5.8">Amo.5.8</ref> as evidence of God's control over the natural world.
Pleiades@Job.9.9-Amo.name: Pleiades

Pochereth-hazzebaim@Ezr.2.57-Neh.description: Pochereth-hazzebaim, a family listed among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
Pochereth-hazzebaim@Ezr.2.57-Neh.name: Pochereth-hazzebaim

Pontus@Act.2.9-1Pe.description: Pontus was a region in Asia Minor along the Black Sea coast, home to Jewish inhabitants and early Christian converts.
Pontus@Act.2.9-1Pe.name: Pontus

Poratha@Est.9.8.description: Poratha, one of the ten sons of Haman, who was hanged along with his brothers after their father's downfall.
Poratha@Est.9.8.name: Poratha

Potiphar@Gen.37.36-.description: Potiphar, the Egyptian officer who purchased Joseph as a slave and later imprisoned him after false accusations by Potiphar's wife.
Potiphar@Gen.37.36-.name: Potiphar

Potiphera@Gen.41.45-.description: Potiphera, the priest of On (Heliopolis), whose daughter Asenath was given to Joseph as a wife by Pharaoh.
Potiphera@Gen.41.45-.name: Potiphera

Potsherd_Gate@Jer.19.2.description: The Potsherd Gate was a gate in Jerusalem near the Valley of Ben Hinnom, where Jeremiah was instructed to proclaim a message of judgment against Judah.
Potsherd_Gate@Jer.19.2.name: Potsherd_Gate

Preparation_Festival@Mat.27.62-Jhn.description: The day of Preparation was the day before the Sabbath (<ref="Mrk.15.42; Luke 23:54">Mrk.15.42; Luke 23:54</ref>) or the day before the Passover (<ref="Jhn.19.14, 31, 42">Jhn.19.14, 31, 42</ref>).
Preparation_Festival@Mat.27.62-Jhn.name: Preparation_Festival

Priscilla@Act.18.2-2Ti.description: Priscilla, also known as Prisca, was a Jewish Christian and the wife of Aquila, who worked with Paul in his ministry and hosted a church in their home.
Priscilla@Act.18.2-2Ti.name: Priscilla

Prochorus@Act.6.5.description: Prochorus, one of the seven men chosen by the early church in Jerusalem to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows.
Prochorus@Act.6.5.name: Prochorus

Puah@Exo.1.15.description: Puah, one of the two Hebrew midwives, along with Shiphrah, who defied Pharaoh's order to kill male Hebrew babies.
Puah@Exo.1.15.name: Puah

Puah@Gen.46.13-1Ch.description: Puah, also known as Puvah, was a son of Issachar and grandson of Jacob, and his descendants were called the Punites.
Puah@Gen.46.13-1Ch.name: Puah

Puah@Jdg.10.1.description: Puah, the son of Dodo from the tribe of Issachar, who's son Tola judged Israel after Abimelech.
Puah@Jdg.10.1.name: Puah

Publius@Act.28.7-.description: Publius, the chief official of Malta, who hosted Paul and his companions for three days after their shipwreck on the island.
Publius@Act.28.7-.name: Publius

Pudens@2Ti.4.21.description: Pudens, a Christian in Rome who sent greetings to Timothy through Paul's letter.
Pudens@2Ti.4.21.name: Pudens

Punon@Num.33.42-.description: Punon was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, located between Zalmonah and Oboth.
Punon@Num.33.42-.name: Punon

Purah@Jdg.7.10-.description: Purah was Gideon's servant who went with him to spy on the Midianite camp.
Purah@Jdg.7.10-.name: Purah

Purim@Est.3.7-.description: Purim is the Jewish festival celebrating the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's plot to destroy them, as recorded in the book of Esther (<ref="Esther 9:26-32">Esther 9:26-32</ref>).
Purim@Est.3.7-.name: Purim

Put@Gen.10.6-1Ch.description: Put was a son of Ham and grandson of Noah.
Put@Gen.10.6-1Ch.name: Put

Puteoli@Act.28.13.description: Puteoli was a major port city in Italy where Paul stayed for seven days on his journey to Rome as a prisoner.
Puteoli@Act.28.13.name: Puteoli

Puthites@1Ch.2.53.description: The Puthites were a clan from the tribe of Judah.
Puthites@1Ch.2.53.name: Puthites

Putiel@Exo.6.25.description: Putiel was the father-in-law of Eleazar, son of Aaron.
Putiel@Exo.6.25.name: Putiel

Pyrrhus@Act.20.4.description: Pyrrhus was a Berean who accompanied Paul on his journey to Asia.
Pyrrhus@Act.20.4.name: Pyrrhus
